input.question: For moving forward in Minecraft, do you want to trigger it with a puff (it keeps moving until you puff again), or by pushing the physical joystick forward?

options.label: Triple puff to start moving, latches on automatically - what you use in 20 of 43 games including 007 - First Light
Push the joystick forward directly - what you use in 15 of 43 games including Flight Simulator

input.question: For moving backward in Minecraft, do you want to trigger it with a sip that toggles on/off, or by pulling the physical joystick back?

options.label: Sip to toggle moving backward on and off - what you use in 21 of 43 games including 007 - First Light
Pull the joystick back directly - what you use in 14 of 43 games including Flight Simulator

input.summary: Settled 14 controls from clear top-ranked history (B, X, Y, left_bumper, right_bumper, left_trigger, right_trigger, left_stick, right_stick, dpad_N, dpad_S, dpad_W, dpad_E, start), all evidenced by their own past bindings for that same output. Left 15 controls unbound (back, guide, and all kb_*/mouse_right_button) because Minecraft Bedrock's sourced control list defines no function for them here - they're keyboard/mouse/console-menu slots with nothing to fire. Asked 2 questions on the two controls where their history splits close to evenly between a mouth-actuated approach and moving the physical joystick directly: forward movement (left_joy_up) and backward movement (left_joy_down), since that choice shapes how they'll play the whole game.
